senses.gloss:
asmitā
(‘sense of “I exist”,’ ‘egoism’)
------------------------------------------
The Yogasūtras of पतञ्जलि (200 B. C.) defines योग as the suppression of the चित्त-vṛttis or the modifications of the मिन्द्. Among these modifications one group is called ‘kliṣta’ (‘the afflicted’). These ‘kleśas’ or afflictions are again listed as five, of which ‘asmitā’ or egoism is the second (2.3). It has been defined as the false identification of the seer or the Self, called dṛkśakti or पुरुष, with the instrument of seeing viz., the बुद्धि (intellect or मिन्द्) (2.6). When the पुरुष who is really asaṅga or unattached and free, thus gets identified with the मिन्द्, he experiences happiness and misery resulting in bondage. Due to this reason अस्मिता is called a क्लेश, an affliction, which is an obstacle to योग.
See also KLEŚAS.

aśmārohaṇa
(‘mounting the stone’)
------------------------------------------
Among all the Hindu सṁस्कारस् or sacraments, विवाह or मर्रिअगे, has been given the central place. Unlike as in some other societies, मर्रिअगे for a Hindu, is not a social contract but a spiritual sacrament and hence considered as perma-nent and indissoluble.
Out of the several steps involved in the sacrament of मर्रिअगे, अश्मारोहण is also one. When the couple go round the nuptial fire three times—this is called agnipariṇayana or circumambulating the fire—the bridegroom makes the bride step upon a mill-stone each time, with certain mantras, the purport of which is that she should be firm and steady like the stone, in her marital life which is spiritual companionship.
See also SAṀSKĀRAS and VIVĀHA.
